BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: review of the Seller's update draft and Disclosure Letter

## 1. Threshold point: the "cleared" and "FINAL" framing

The cover materials say the [STANDARD] clauses are "cleared by both sides", the package was "settled at principal level", and the review "may proceed on that basis". None of this is confirmed through our authority process, so I have reviewed every clause and treat none as agreed. The "market standard" claims are the Seller's assertion, not evidence. The [STANDARD] label covers almost every provision that departs from our playbook, so skipping those clauses would mean skipping the real issues.

The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also undercuts its cover narrative. It admits that Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment and discharge, and the bonus funding are all outstanding, and that title is not independently verified.

## 2. Departures from the playbook

| Item | Seller draft | Our position | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Open at 25% / AUD 6m | The Seller's number is our conditional fallback, which needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority naming this draft. None exists. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x our position. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, first dollar once exceeded | 5x our position, and the structure is wrong (a deductible instead of a tipping basket). |
| Claims period (12.3) | 18 months | 24 months | 18 months is a fallback needing Frost's written approval, which has not been given. |
| Title/capacity (Fundamental) | Same caps and time limits as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cut title protection. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these | Reject. This is a hidden override of the carve-out. No one on our side can waive it. |
| Limitation "applies to all Claims unless expressly stated" (12.3 / 13) | General regime overrides by default | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate | Reject. This is the hidden general-regime override the playbook prohibits. |
| Disclosure (Sch 7, Letter 1.1–1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Reject all deemed disclosure. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Bars claims for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew or could discover from the data room or public records | Delete | Delete. It also catches title, capacity, fraud and indemnities. |

**Why the numbers matter together.** The 4.8m cap looks like a single concession, but combined with a 250k excess-only basket, a 25k de minimis, an 18-month window, and data-room-wide disclosure and knowledge bars, recoverable value is far below 4.8m. Even if the cap were authorised, matching a fallback number does not clear the package. Each term is judged separately and requires its own written authority.

**Possible Seller responses.** If the Seller argues the 20% cap and 18 months are "agreed", point out that no written authority has been given. If the Seller wants to trade, any movement must go to Amelia Frost first, identifying this draft.

## 3. Deal-specific issues

**Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue)**
- The draft offers reasonable endeavours, with consent treated as satisfied "on delivery" of the counterparty's written consent.
- We need an effective consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a real condition.
- The Seller's letter (para 2) concedes it has neither. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.

**Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m outstanding)**
- The draft offers a post-completion release.
- We need a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases (for example PPSR discharge) at Completion.
- A post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Frost's approval. Neither exists.
- The Seller's letter (para 3) confirms the facility is unpaid and there is no discharge.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000)**
- The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" and it is not itemised in the funds flow.
- The funds flow must show it as a specific line item, or the Seller must fund it.
- Payroll tax, superannuation and other triggered on-costs must be covered too. The Seller's letter (para 5) does not say whether they apply, so we should ask rather than assume.
- The assertion that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" should be rejected, since no mechanics are agreed.

**Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010)**
- The existing indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment and the Seller calls it adequate. Broaden it (for example to claims over ownership or use of the project materials and related costs) while preserving the SOW3 cure mechanism (payment of the fees, then transfer of materials).
- The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction. DD-010 is not bank verification, and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. Neither accept nor dispute the figure. Request payment evidence and the assignment.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". We should not adopt that characterisation, and equally should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any dollar figure.
- Ask for log preservation, a documented investigation, regular updates and cooperation covenants. Keep this as a separate regime.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000, three at AUD 110,000)**
- "Ordinary-course operating costs" is the Seller's label. The Letter (para 8) itself does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Request the contracts, termination rights and commitment dates, then assess. There should be no automatic Debt classification or price deduction, and we should not accept the Seller's characterisation either.

**Tax and IP**
- The Seller treats them as "settled under the general regime". They remain OPEN.
- Do not accept the general regime for them. Equally, do not assume any unlimited liability or any resolution.

**Title**
- The Seller relies on the DD-012 register, but that is a Company-supplied internal source, not independent proof. Letter para 10 concedes we have not verified it.
- Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Examples are ASIC extracts, the share transfer history, PPSR and encumbrance searches (including any Riverlark security over shares), and Seller authority documents.
- Using public registers to verify is fine. Treating them as deemed disclosure is not.

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The Letter says neither is described as requiring consent to a share sale. That is the Seller's description, not our conclusion. Have the team check the underlying clauses before treating them as non-issues.

## 4. Recommendations

1. **Reply that no [STANDARD], FINAL or "agreed" labels are accepted.** State that the whole package is subject to Wattlebridge's mark-up.
2. **Re-set the liability package to our opening positions:**
   - 25% / AUD 6m cap
   - AUD 5k de minimis
   - AUD 50k first-dollar basket
   - 24-month claims period
3. **Do not offer or signal the 20% and 18-month fallbacks.** If the deal team wants to use them, it needs Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the specific draft first.
4. **Restore a separate Fundamental/Title regime:** 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Add an unqualified fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out** from caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
6. **Delete clause 8.3.** If the Seller needs a qualifier, limit it to Seller knowledge with named knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Replace general disclosure with specific fair disclosure.** Strike Letter paras 1.1–1.2 as deemed disclosure.
8. **Make Bluefen and Riverlark true Completion deliverables:**
   - Bluefen: effective consent plus evidence its conditions are met.
   - Riverlark: payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective releases.
9. **Put the AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs in the funds flow as a specific line item, or make them Seller-funded.** Ask the Seller to confirm the on-cost position.
10. **Broaden the Ironquay indemnity** while preserving the SOW3 cure, and request payment evidence. Keep the AUD 180k unverified.
11. **Add incident covenants for DD-006** (preservation, investigation, updates), with no assumed breach and no numbers.
12. **Run a diligence request list:** Sandbar contracts, lease and Mossvale clauses, and independent title and encumbrance evidence.
13. **Keep Tax, IP, Title, payment and covenant provisions as separate regimes, with Tax/IP left open.**

I can draft the response letter to Seller's counsel and a clause-by-clause mark-up next. I can also prepare a short escalation note for Amelia Frost on the fallback positions, if the team wants to consider them.
